# F#

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from fsharp/lang.json and fsharp/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check F# code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- init --apply
```

For a F# project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small F# package from [`fsharp/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/fsharp/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//fsharp:defs.bzl", "fsharp_library", "fsharp_test")

fsharp_library(
    name = "my_project",
    # do not sort: F# compile order, dependencies first
    srcs = ["Greet.fs"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

fsharp_test(
    name = "greet_test",
    size = "small",
    srcs = ["GreetTest.fs"],
    deps = [":my_project"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Dependencies

### Compile order

F# compiles files in the order you list them. List `srcs` in that order and
tell buildifier not to sort the list:

```python
fsharp_library(
    name = "order_lib",
    srcs = [
        # buildifier: disable=sort
        "Helper.fs",
        "Demo.fs",
    ],
    deps = ["@nuget//fsharp.core"],
)
```

`dx generate` works out the order from the sources. It does not read
`.fsproj` files. A file comes after every sibling it uses:

- a type, exception or nested module that a sibling declares, named plainly
  (`{ b: Item }`) or qualified (`Helper.suffix`);
- a sibling's file-level module (`module Demo.Types`), by `open` or by name;
- a sibling found by `open`, matched by file name.

A `Name.fsi` signature file goes right before its `Name.fs`. A `.fsi` without
a matching `.fs` fails. When two files need each other, generation stops and
names one edge, for example `A.fs -> B.fs (B)`. Split the directory or list
`srcs` by hand. The `fsharp/tests/fixtures/adopt_fsharp` tree shows a full
run.

### NuGet packages

List your packages in a `paket.dependencies` file. `dx update --apply` locks
them into `nuget.lock.json`. Then declare the lock in your `MODULE.bazel`:

```python
nuget = use_extension("@rules_dx//csharp:extensions.bzl", "nuget")
nuget.lock(
    name = "nuget",
    lock = "//third_party/dotnet:nuget.lock.json",
)
use_repo(nuget, "nuget")
```

Depend on a package as `@nuget//<lowercase package id>`. `dx update nuget`
moves the pins to newer versions.

## Quality

`fantomas` formats, `fsharplint` lints and `fsc` typechecks. dx fetches all
three, so you install nothing:

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- format //app/...
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- lint //app/...
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- typecheck //app/...
```

`fsc` compiles each target a second time with the pinned F# compiler and
reports its `FS` diagnostics. See the
[quality config table](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/cli/commands/quality.md).

## Coverage

`bazel coverage` and `dx coverage` run F# tests under coverlet and write LCOV.
They cover the first-party assemblies that match `--instrumentation_filter`.
The test assembly counts only with `--instrument_test_targets`. Tag a test
`no-coverage` to skip it under coverage.

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//fsharp:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fsharp:defs.bzl", "fsharp_library", "fsharp_binary", "fsharp_test")
```

### `fsharp_library`

```python
fsharp_library(name, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over fsharp_library; srcs compile in list order, target_frameworks defaults to net10.0 and warnings are errors.

### `fsharp_binary`

```python
fsharp_binary(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, upstream_visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Binary with target_frameworks net10.0, warnings as errors following the repo config, srcs compiled in list order.

### `fsharp_test`

```python
fsharp_test(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Test with target_frameworks net10.0, warnings as errors following the repo config, size small; srcs compiled in list order.

### `fsharp_bench`

```python
fsharp_bench(name, *, srcs, deps = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

An fsharp_test that runs the [<Benchmark>] classes in srcs with BenchmarkDotNet and writes dx-bench.json.

### `fsharp_fuzz_test`

```python
fsharp_fuzz_test(name, *, srcs, deps = None, visibility = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

A SharpFuzz harness and a `<name>_run` runner for `dx fuzz`; the first-party libraries in deps are instrumented. Linux and macOS only.

### `fsharp_doc_shard`

```python
fsharp_doc_shard(name, library, package = "", **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one F# library.

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for F#:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `fantomas`, `fsc`, `fsharplint` |
| Ecosystems | nuget |
| Manifests | `paket.dependencies` |
| Lockfiles | `paket.lock` |

## Platforms

F# builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- macOS arm64
- Windows arm64
- Windows x86_64

See the [support matrix](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/support-matrix.md).

## API docs

`tools/dx docs` builds the API docs with `fsharp doc driver`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

To declare a docs target yourself, load the rule behind it:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fsharp:defs.bzl", "fsharp_doc_shard")
```
